caption: Intensity of the $\mu = 4$ slab mode ($n_R = 2\pi$, $Q = 19.57$), normalized to its value at the right cavity face. Outside the cavity the QNM intensity grows as $e^{\gamma_f x}$ with $\gamma_f = 0.102\,L^{-1}$; continued with the real wavenumber it stays constant. The shaded bands mark the cavity and a perturbing layer at $d = 8L$.
Real part of the shift of the $\mu = 4$ mode versus gap at $\delta = 10^{-3}$: exact pole and the naive, regularized, self-consistent and resummed schemes.
Imaginary part of the shift for the configuration of Fig. 2. Negative values correspond to a larger radiative loss.

Deviation of the Lorentzian estimate of the resonance position from the exact pole, in units of the exact linewidth $|\mathrm{Im}\,k|$, for $\delta = 0.01$ and $0.1$. Open symbols mark fits rejected by the window-stability criterion (halving the fit window moves the centre by more than $1\%$ of $\gamma_0$).

Magnitude of the shift of the $\mu = 4$ mode at $\delta = 10^{-4}$. The exact shift grows at $(0.1029 \pm 0.0004)\,L^{-1}$ for $d \ge 8L$, against the field rate $\gamma_f = 0.1022\,L^{-1}$ that sets the growth of the naive shift. The regularized shift stays bounded.

Relative errors of the perturbative schemes for the $\mu = 4$ mode at $\delta = 10^{-3}$ (coloured lines) and the parameter-free predictions of Eqs. (13), (16) and (18) (black dashed): $|a(d)F|$ for the naive scheme, $|(\alpha + b e^{-2in_B\tilde kd})F|$ for the self-consistent scheme, $|bR\rho_p^{(1)}|$ for the resummed scheme and the floor $|1 - ce^{-\gamma_f d}|$ for the regularized scheme. With the second Born term included, the resummed error is of third order.

Second-order coefficient $a(d)$ with the linear propagation term removed, from exact poles computed in 40-digit arithmetic at $\delta = 10^{-9}$ (symbols) and from Eq. (14) (lines). The largest relative deviation over the 48 gaps is $5.0\times10^{-7}$. The oscillation is the second Born term, which decays as $e^{-\gamma_f d}$ about the constant $a_\infty = \alpha + 2in_BL_pE/(E - 1)$.

Magnitudes of the four terms of the second-order coefficient, Eq. (14), for the $\mu = 4$ mode. The background term $\alpha$ dominates below $d \approx |\alpha|/(2n_B) = 10\,L$ and the propagation term beyond. The second Born term nearly cancels the background term at contact and decays as $e^{-\gamma_f d}$.

Small-strength limit of the regularized-scheme error for the $\mu = 4$ mode (median over $\delta \le 4.6\times10^{-4}$) against the floor law of Eq. (18), $|1 - ce^{-\gamma_f d}|$ with $|c - 1| = 5.11\times10^{-3}$, and its thin-layer form. The measured floor agrees with Eq. (18) to within $2.8\%$ at every gap.

Relative error versus strength $\delta$ at $d = 0.54\,L$ for the $\mu = 4$ mode. The naive, self-consistent and resummed errors are proportional to $\delta$, the resummed error with the second Born term to $\delta^2$, and the regularized error is set by its floor.

As Fig. 10 at $d = 20.1\,L$. The errors of the naive and self-consistent schemes are larger than at small gaps by the growth of $|a(d)F|$, whereas the resummed errors are unchanged; beyond $\delta \approx 10^{-2}$ all single-mode schemes fail.
Relative error of the naive first-order scheme over the gap and strength plane ($\mu = 4$). The black contour marks 10% error; crosses mark cells where the minimal-loss and continued poles differ.
As Fig. 12 for the regularized first-order scheme. Its error is bounded but exceeds 10% for every strength once $d \gtrsim 1\,L$.
As Fig. 12 for the self-consistent scheme. Grey cells: no fixed point found.
As Fig. 12 for the resummed scheme with the exact background ratio $\alpha$. Grey cells: no fixed point found.

Smallest gap $d_c$ at which each scheme exceeds 10% relative error, versus strength, for the $\mu = 4$ mode. A missing point means that the scheme stays below 10% on the whole grid ($d \le 30\,L$); a point at $d = 0.05\,L$ means it exceeds 10% already at the smallest gap.

Absolute error of the naive scheme divided by the second-order prediction $|a(d)F^2|$, versus the gap in units of the field decay length, for three cavities spanning a factor 14 in $\gamma_f$. Each strength is chosen so that $|a(d)F| = 0.01$ at the largest gap.
Absolute error of the naive scheme divided by the second-order prediction $|a(d)F^2|$ of Eq. (13) for five layer thicknesses and both signs of the permittivity change ($\mu = 4$, $\delta = 10^{-5}$).

Distance from the continued $\mu = 4$ pole to the nearest other pole within $0.45\,L^{-1}$, in units of the shift, for $\delta = 10^{-3}$ and $0.1$. Open symbols mark gaps where the pole with the smallest loss is not the continued pole.

Relative error of the embedding-basis RSE pole versus basis size at $d = 0.5\,L$ for four strengths ($\mu = 4$), each with the basis permittivity and margin that give the smallest error at $N = 401$. The dotted line shows $N^{-3}$ for reference.

Deep truncation of the RSE for the four configurations with the largest error at $N = 401$, all at $d = 3\,L$. The dotted line marks the target relative error of $10^{-6}$, which every configuration reaches from $N = 801$.
